records.name: Park Friends Network (Fairmount Park Conservancy)
records.summary: A citywide network of neighborhood park groups, more than 140 of them, that clean up, plant, and garden in Philadelphia parks. The Conservancy and the city help run it, and joining a local group is the usual way in.
records.what_you_do: Join a park friends group near you for regular cleanups and planting, or sign up for the spring Love Your Park Week service days.

cost.text: Not stated on the pages checked

first_step.how: Find a park friends group near you through loveyourpark.org, or call 215-988-9334 to ask how to get on a group's list
first_step.basis: The network says anyone can learn about a local group by joining a service project, so the way in is public

records.notes: The Oct 7, 2026 Love Your Park registration item gives no event date on the page. The network does not publish one list of all groups, so each local group still needs its own check.

records.name: Friends of Pastorius Park
records.summary: Volunteers who look after Pastorius Park in Chestnut Hill: they care for its plantings, waterways, and historic structures, and work with the city's parks department.
records.what_you_do: Help with workdays that clear invasive plants and plant native trees and shrubs that support birds and pollinators.

cost.text: No cost is mentioned for volunteering or visiting

first_step.how: Sign up for the volunteer opportunities newsletter (the site says only a few emails a year) or email info@friendsofpastorius.org
first_step.basis: The page does not say how workdays are announced beyond the newsletter, so the way in is unclear

records.notes: The only dated item on the site is a 2021 amphitheater restoration, and no 2025 or 2026 events are listed. The copyright footer is not counted as evidence. The volunteer page was not fetched.

records.name: Chestnut Hill Tree Tenders
records.summary: A volunteer group in Chestnut Hill that plants free street trees twice a year, supported by the Chestnut Hill Community Association and the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society.
records.what_you_do: Deliver and plant street trees on planting days, and help the tree committee. Households that get a tree agree to water it and give volunteers access on planting day.

first_step.how: Contact one of the co-chairs listed on the page to volunteer, or apply for a tree online through the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society
first_step.basis: Volunteers join by contacting a co-chair, and the page describes planting days openly

records.notes: The page gives an application deadline of Nov 1, 2025 and a planting day of April 12 with no year. Co-chair contact details are on the page and were not copied here. No training schedule is listed.

records.name: Philly Tree People
records.summary: A volunteer-led nonprofit that plants and cares for trees in East Kensington, Kensington, and Fishtown (ZIP codes 19125 and 19134).
records.what_you_do: Join tree planting days, a pruning club, a pit care club, or tree checking, or request a tree through the site.

cost.text: Volunteer cost is not listed; the group asks for donations

first_step.how: Subscribe through the Get in touch page, or email phillytreepeople@phillytreepeople.org to ask about a volunteer role
first_step.basis: Each volunteer role has its own learn more page, and a micro volunteering option is listed, though the sign-up steps are not described

records.notes: The page lists a spring planting on 2/19/2026 and a fall 2026 tree request with a 5/1/2026 deadline, which has passed. A February 2026 planting is the newest dated evidence.

records.name: TreePhilly Volunteer Giveaways (Parks and Recreation)
records.summary: The city's tree program, run by Parks and Recreation, holds citywide tree giveaways with volunteer shifts that residents can sign up to help with.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a volunteer shift at a citywide giveaway, where you help hand out and plant trees.

schedule.text: Citywide giveaway shifts from 10 am to 2:30 pm on weekends, including Sept 19 and Nov 8, 2026

cost.text: The trees are given away free

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form linked on the TreePhilly page for the giveaway you want
first_step.basis: Each giveaway has its own sign-up form, and the volunteer shifts do not have a ZIP code limit

records.notes: Some giveaways limit tree pickup to certain ZIP codes. Those limits apply to residents picking up trees, not to the volunteer shifts. Several October 2026 giveaways are listed.

records.name: Schuylkill Center for Environmental Education
records.summary: A nature center in Roxborough with woods, fields, and trails. Volunteers help with its yearly Winter Bird Census and with seasonal work days.
records.what_you_do: Count birds during the Winter Bird Census, or join a volunteer day such as the Greenhouse Decorators event.

cost.text: The Winter Bird Census is free

first_step.how: Use the Sign Up link on the event page, or call 215-482-7300 to ask about volunteer days
first_step.basis: The Winter Bird Census is for birders of any experience level and includes a sign-up link

records.notes: The Winter Bird Census page covers Feb 8, 2025 (adults only); the 2026 date was not shown. The home page lists a Greenhouse Decorators volunteer day on Saturday, Oct 10, 2026. Stream monitoring was not confirmed.

records.name: Riverfront North Partnership
records.summary: A nonprofit that cares for the 11-mile Northeast Philadelphia Greenway along the Delaware River, which connects neighbors to the river and to parks. It invites volunteers to help.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on the greenway and in its parks through the group's volunteer page.

locations.label: Northeast Philadelphia Greenway and Delaware River parks

cost.text: The volunteer cost is not stated; some events are free

first_step.how: Email info@riverfrontnorth.org or call 215-425-8350, or use the volunteer page on the website
first_step.basis: The page lists no volunteer days or schedule, so the way in is unclear

records.notes: The page prints no event dates. A Bridesburg item has no stated date, and a Learn to Fish event is free and first come, first served. Tree planting and cleanup days were not confirmed on the pages checked.

records.name: Friends of the Wissahickon
records.summary: The group that helps care for the 2,000-acre Wissahickon Valley Park in Northwest Philadelphia, with volunteer service days, individual stewardship, planting, and guided outings.
records.what_you_do: Join a volunteer service day or do individual stewardship work, and go on hikes and planting events in the valley.

cost.text: Not stated on the home page

first_step.how: Visit the Volunteer Service Days page on the website, or call 215-247-0417
first_step.basis: The site has a dedicated service days page, but the sign-up method was not on the pages checked

records.notes: A news post is dated Oct 8, 2026. Event listings for Oct 10 show no year. The volunteer service days page was not fetched, so the schedule is unknown.

records.name: Ocean Blue Project Philadelphia River Cleanups
records.summary: A national group that runs trash cleanups on Philadelphia's rivers and creeks, including the Delaware waterfront, the Schuylkill River Trail, Penn's Landing, and Fairmount Park riverbanks.
records.what_you_do: Pick up litter along the riverbanks during cleanups that usually last 1 to 2 hours, held rain or shine.

locations.label: Delaware River waterfront, Schuylkill River Trail, Penn's Landing, Fairmount Park riverbanks

schedule.text: Cleanups throughout the year, usually 1 to 2 hours, rain or shine

cost.text: No participation fee is stated; gloves, bags, and tools are provided

first_step.how: Find a listed Philadelphia river cleanup on the national cleanup events page
first_step.basis: Cleanups are listed publicly and supplies are provided

records.notes: The page lists no dated event. The organizer is based in Virginia, and individual Philadelphia cleanup listings were not checked.

records.name: Schuylkill Banks
records.summary: The nonprofit behind the Schuylkill River Trail, which covers the southernmost eight miles of the river from the Fairmount Dam to the Delaware. It runs public trail events and links to a volunteer page.
records.what_you_do: Take part in public trail events, or ask about volunteer work through the volunteer page.

locations.label: Schuylkill River Trail, Fairmount Dam to the Delaware River

cost.text: Not stated on the page checked

first_step.how: Visit the volunteer page on the website, or call 215-309-5523 to ask about volunteer days
first_step.basis: The volunteer page was linked but its schedule and sign-up steps were not on the page checked

records.notes: Kayak tours, movie nights, and riverboat tours are public events, not volunteer shifts. No dated volunteer day was confirmed. The organization is the Schuylkill River Development Corporation.

records.name: Pennypack Ecological Restoration Trust
records.summary: A nature preserve trust that buys, restores, and protects about 900 acres in the Pennypack watershed in southeastern Montgomery County.
records.notes: The preserve is in Montgomery County, not in the city. Pennypack Park inside Philadelphia is a separate place. The trust's Streamkeepers and ReForesters volunteer programs were not checked, so a city resident could still ask whether they welcome volunteers from Philadelphia.

leads_only.name: Friends of Gold Star Park
leads_only.note: Featured in an April 2024 city post about a Park Friends group that does clean-ups, concerts, and Earth Day events. The group's own website was not found or checked.

leads_only.name: Cobbs Creek Park Ambassadors
leads_only.note: Named on a Penn Sustainability event page for a January 2026 cleanup. The group's own page was not found, and the event may already have passed.

leads_only.name: Philly Forest Stewards
leads_only.note: City program for long-term volunteers who adopt sections of natural land. The page is a 2020 post; current status not checked.

notes: Verdict counts: publish 10, out_of_area 1. Six of ten searches used, 17 fetches used; budget not exhausted. Several records (Friends of Pastorius Park, Ocean Blue Project, Schuylkill Banks, Riverfront North) are thin on dates and volunteer detail and should be treated as low or medium confidence. Delaware Riverkeeper Network was checked and left out: its office is in Bristol, PA, its pages do not list Philadelphia volunteer or citizen science programs, and it is a regional group rather than a Philadelphia one. The Philadelphia Mid-Winter Bird Census is a citywide event, not a group, and its DVOC page was blocked. Nature-environment groups in the city are mostly reached through the Park Friends Network, so the family is thin on neighborhood-specific groups.
